title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
facts: Researchers from Imperial College London analyzed English National Diabetes Audit data from 2011 to 2024.
The study found type 2 diabetes diagnoses decreased among adults aged 60 to 79 while rising in adults under 40.
The sharpest increase in new type 2 diabetes diagnoses occurred among women in their 20s and white women in their 30s.
The research study on young-onset diabetes was published in The Lancet Regional Health Europe journal.
Shivani Misra is a clinical associate professor for diabetes at Imperial College London.
Baptist Gallwitz serves as an endocrinologist and spokesperson for the German Diabetes Society (DDG).
Type 2 diabetes diagnoses among German youth aged 11 to 17 increased by 5.8% annually between 2014 and 2023.
Helen Kirrane represents the charity organization Diabetes UK.
The German Diabetes Society advocates for a tiered value-added tax system exempting fresh produce from sales tax.
The German Diabetes Society recommends incorporating one hour of mandatory physical activity into school schedules daily.
Alexandra Kautzky-Willer directs the division for endocrinology and metabolism at the Medical University of Vienna.
Alexandra Kautzky-Willer published research in Deutsches Ärzteblatt indicating type 2 diabetes is underdiagnosed in women.
Fasting blood sugar measurements measure glucose levels after eight hours of fasting.
HbA1c diagnostic tests calculate an individual's average blood sugar levels over a two- to three-month period.
Standard health insurance in Germany and Austria covers fasting blood sugar tests but excludes routine coverage for oral glucose tolerance and HbA1c screening.
